topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Frequent Keeping
explanation: The memory hierarchy organizes storage levels based on access speed, capacity, and cost, positioning faster, smaller caches (SRAM) closer to the CPU and slower, larger main memory (DRAM) further away. Caching strategies exploit the principles of temporal and spatial locality to minimize the average memory access time (AMAT). By proactively moving frequently referenced data blocks from a slower level to a faster cache, the system increases the cache hit rate. Effective management of this hierarchy is crucial for maximizing processor throughput and minimizing memory latency penalties.
